blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — More areas in the country are expected to experience drought from October 2026 to March 2027 as El Niño persists, the state weather bureau said Wednesday. In its climate outlook, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said below-normal rainfall is likely during the period, according to weather specialist Junie Ruiz. Pagasa recently declared the end of southwest monsoon or “habagat” season and observed weaker winds and declining rainfall associated with the weather system.
